sourcedFrom: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere (UNDATED — no copyright year is printed anywhere in the document)
cleanIntro: Kel-Tec's own disassembly for the PF-9, then the cleaning it calls for. The strip lives on printed p.13, which is a scanned plate inside an otherwise readable book — it is quoted here from the OCR of that plate, hash and tool on record.

steps.title: Magazine out, then the chamber
steps.action: Remove the magazine, then briskly pull the slide back to extract the round in the chamber.
steps.prose: Magazine first, every time. Pull the slide briskly rather than easing it — a slow pull is how a live round gets left half-extracted.
steps.quote: To unload the pistol, remove the magazine and briskly pull the slide back to extract the round in the chamber.
steps.cite: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere — Unloading, printed p.11
steps.warn: Never touch the trigger when working the slide.

steps.title: Keep the port clear and look into the chamber
steps.action: Do not obstruct the ejection port and keep your fingers away from the trigger and the muzzle, then visually inspect the chamber to make sure it is empty.
steps.prose: A hand over the port is the usual reason a round does not leave the gun. Look at the chamber — do not take the extractor's word for it.
steps.quote: Do not obstruct the ejector port and keep fingers away from trigger and muzzle. Visually inspect the chamber to make sure it is empty.
steps.cite: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere — Unloading, printed p.11

steps.title: Empty the magazine as well
steps.action: Push the remaining cartridges in the magazine forward and out.
steps.prose: Forward and out over the feed lips, one at a time. The magazine is part of the clearing, not an afterthought.
steps.quote: Push the remaining cartridges in the magazine forward and out.
steps.cite: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere — Unloading, printed p.11

steps.title: Lock the slide open
steps.action: With the pistol unloaded, pull the slide back and push up the slide stop until the slide is locked open.
steps.prose: The PF-9's slide stop is pushed up by hand here; the gun is not going to hold it for you on an empty magazine well.
steps.quote: Unload your pistol. Pull the slide back and push up the slide stop until the slide is locked open.
steps.cite: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere — Disassembly, printed p.13

steps.title: Pull the assembly pin with a case rim
steps.action: Using the rim of a cartridge case, pull the assembly pin out of the pistol.
steps.prose: The case rim is the tool Kel-Tec specifies — it fits the pin's groove and will not mark the frame the way a screwdriver blade does.
steps.quote: Using the rim of a case, pull the assembly pin from the pistol.
steps.cite: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere — Disassembly, printed p.13

steps.title: Ease the slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Holding the slide, release the slide stop and allow the slide to move slowly forward, off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: Hold it. With the assembly pin out there is nothing to stop the slide leaving the frame under spring pressure.
steps.quote: While holding the slide, release the slide stop allowing the slide to slowly move forward, off the frame.
steps.cite: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere — Disassembly, printed p.13

steps.title: Recoil spring and barrel out — and stop there
steps.action: Take the recoil spring and barrel out of the slide. That is the end of the disassembly Kel-Tec publishes: no further disassembly is recommended.
steps.prose: Four parts and the magazine. The bound is the manufacturer's, printed on the same page as the strip itself.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring and barrel. No further disassembly is recommended.
steps.cite: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere — Disassembly, printed p.13

steps.title: Never loosen the extractor spring screw
steps.action: Leave the extractor spring screw alone. Kel-Tec prints the prohibition immediately after the strip, and separately warns that dry firing can damage the firing pin and that same extractor spring screw.
steps.prose: It is the one fastener on the slide that looks like an invitation, and it is the one the manual singles out.
steps.quote: Do not loosen the extractor spring screw.
steps.cite: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere — Disassembly, printed p.13
steps.warn: Do not dry fire the pistol — Kel-Tec states it can damage the firing pin and extractor spring screw.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly and magazine. This is the disassembly Kel-Tec points you at when routine cleaning is not enough.
steps.prose: The manual's own maintenance section treats this strip as the deeper option, not as a separate exercise.
steps.quote: For a more detailed cleaning, the pistol should be disassembled as described in the section "Disassembly"
steps.cite: Kel-Tec PF-9 Pistol Safety, Instruction, and Parts Manual — REV 0606 — printed on the parts drawing page only (printed p.9); no revision code on the cover or elsewhere — Maintenance, printed p.14

deepAbsentReason: Kel-Tec's PF-9 manual ends its disassembly with "Remove the recoil spring and barrel. No further disassembly is recommended" (printed p.13) and immediately forbids loosening the extractor spring screw. The only further procedure the book publishes at all is MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY (printed p.14), which is a magazine job rather than a deeper strip of the pistol and is carried in the cleaning list below. So this listing has NO deep clean — that is the manual's answer, not a gap in ours.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Brush the barrel bore and chamber with a good powder removing solvent and bore brush
Wipe the areas clean with patches or a swab

cleaning.name: BREECH, EXTRACTOR AND FRAME
tasks: With a small brush dipped in solvent, remove all deposits from around the breech of the barrel, the chamber, the extractor and the adjacent areas exposed to powder and primer residue
Remove any residue on the frame with light brushing and a solvent
Do not loosen the extractor spring screw while cleaning around it

cleaning.name: OIL AND WIPE DOWN
tasks: After cleaning the entire gun, use a cloth to apply a light coating of high quality gun oil to all external surfaces, then wipe clean

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE (KEL-TEC'S OWN PROCEDURE)
tasks: Hold the magazine firmly with the bottom facing away from you, and keep a hand or thumb over the spring bottom plate — the spring is under pressure and can fly out
Insert a small punch a quarter inch into the hole in the centre of the bottom plate, pushing down on the spring bottom plate
Slide the bottom plate off with your thumb while holding the spring, then slowly remove the magazine spring and spring bottom plate; the follower should fall out easily
Clean the components and reassemble in reverse

reassembly: Insert the barrel into the slide, push the recoil spring guide with springs into the hole provided in the slide, and hook the base of the recoil spring guide onto the half-moon cutout in the barrel.
Make certain the barrel and recoil springs are well centred before putting them back in the slide.
Push the slide onto the frame until the back lines up with the grip — if it does not go on easily, check that the hammer is half-cocked and that the barrel and recoil spring guide are centred.
Pushing down on the top of the barrel, pull the slide back all the way to compress the recoil springs and push up on the slide stop to hold it.
Look into the assembly pin hole, align it with the cut in the barrel, and insert the assembly pin until it snaps onto the spring.
Pull the slide back a little to release the slide stop, then release the slide.
fncheck: Kel-Tec's own check after assembly: work the slide a few times to check the action. Do not dry fire the pistol — the manual states it can damage the firing pin and extractor spring screw.
